title: Singapore's Stance on Proposal for UN Membership for Palestine and Assistance for Rebuilding of Palestine
what_it_is: Singapore's Stance on Proposal for UN Membership for Palestine and Assistance for Rebuilding of Palestine

sections.label: Questions on Palestine recognition and assistance
sections.summary: Questions ask about Singapore's technical assistance to Palestinian officials, other contributions to a two-state solution, and what prevents recognising Palestine.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Foreign Affairs (a) how effective has Singapore's technical assistance to Palestinian officials been in helping the Palestinian Authority to function more effectively as a state; (b) what other contribution is Singapore making towards realising a two-state solution with the Israelis and Palestinians living side-by-side in peace and security; and (c) what prevents Singapore from officially recognising the State of Palestine before a two-state solution is reached.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Foreign Affairs whether Singapore has any plans to train Palestinian officials from Gaza towards aiding in the reconstruction of the enclave once military operations have ceased.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Foreign Affairs in light of the votes by the United Nations (UN) General Assembly on a resolution to support the admission of Palestine as a UN member and the subsequent actions by certain European Union states to recognise Palestine as a state in May 2024 (a) whether it is timely for Singapore to recognise Palestine as a state; and (b) if so, what are the considerations in doing so.

sections.label: UN Security Council veto on Palestine
sections.summary: On 18 April 2024, a UN Security Council resolution recommending Palestine's admission to the UN was vetoed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: On 18 April 2024, a UN Security Council resolution that recommended that Palestine be admitted for membership to the UN was vetoed.

sections.label: Singapore prepared in principle to recognise
sections.summary: Singapore's UN General Assembly vote means Singapore is prepared in principle to recognise the State of Palestine.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Our vote at the UN's General Assembly means that Singapore is prepared in principle to recognise the State of Palestine.

sections.label: Engagement and Enhanced Technical Assistance Package
sections.summary: Singapore will continue engaging the Palestinian Authority and implementing its S$10 million Enhanced Technical Assistance Package to build capacity and prepare for statehood.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Singapore will continue our engagement with the Palestinian Authority.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We will continue to implement our S$10 million Enhanced Technical Assistance Package (ETAP) to help the Palestinian Authority build capacity and to prepare for eventual statehood.

sections.label: Conditions for recognising Palestine
sections.summary: Singapore is prepared in principle to recognise Palestine at an appropriate moment, requiring an effective Palestinian government that renounces terrorism and accepts Israel's right to exist.

sentences.text: So, I would say that we are not going to lock ourselves into a specific time or to whether or not other countries have made decisions in parallel on the same fundamental question.
We are prepared, in principle, to recognise the state of Palestine.

But we want to do so at an appropriate moment when it is helpful, and you must have an effective Palestine government and one, which I alluded to earlier, which must categorically renounce terrorism and must accept the right of Israel to exist.

sections.label: Belief in negotiated two-state solution
sections.summary: Singapore's principal consideration is its long-held belief in a negotiated two-state solution.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: In the case of Singapore, I said our principal consideration is that we have always believed in a negotiated two-state solution.

sections.label: Gaza aid and fundraising
sections.summary: Singapore has delivered three tranches of humanitarian assistance to Gaza, including RSAF airdrops, and Singaporeans have raised at least $15.5 million.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I have not computed the value of the scholarships and we intend to give more.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We have delivered three tranches of humanitarian assistance so far, including deploying the Republic of Singapore Air Force to airdrop, I think, at least 20 tonnes, to Gaza in March.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I should also say that the fundraising from Singaporeans – and I want to give a special shout-out to Rahmatan Lil Alamin – I think we have collectively raised at least $15.5 million so far.

sections.label: Arms sales and UN sanctions
sections.summary: Singapore complies strictly with international obligations on arms sales and UN sanctions and embargoes, submitting regular reports to the UN Register of Conventional Arms.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Singapore complies strictly with our international obligations on international arms sales as well as UN sanctions and embargoes against any country, including submitting regular reports to the UN Register of Conventional Arms, which is a public record which you can access for yourself.

sections.label: Two-state solution position
sections.summary: Singapore's long-standing position is that only a negotiated two-state solution will lead to peace, requiring both sides to recognise the other's right to exist and renounce terrorism.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: That is a separate question from is there a recognisable Palestinian state?

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: And without locking ourselves in prematurely, which may be unhelpful, I am saying that our long-standing position is that only a negotiated two-state solution will lead to a just, durable and comprehensive peace, and both sides must recognise the other's right to exist and must renounce terrorism.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Without those prerequisites, never mind the diplomatic and legal niceties, without the recognition and respect of the other's right to exist and without renouncing terrorism, these cycles of violence will recur.

sections.label: Diplomacy track record
sections.summary: Being welcomed by all sides, including warring parties, requires a track record of principled, deliberate, careful diplomacy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: To be able to welcomed by all sides, including warring parties, requires a track record of principled, deliberate, careful diplomacy.
